v1.feedback: Strong concept — the Lorenz butterfly losing its grip and particles lifting like Saraceno lanterns is a genuine narrative surprise on the parent attractor. Palette (smoke/bone/rust/amber) is restrained and appropriate. Two concerns: with 100K additively-blended particles, the float phase risks washing out into a bright undifferentiated glow — consider capping per-particle alpha lower during the lift (e.g. multiply by `1.0 - uAntiGrav * 0.3`) so individual trajectories remain legible. Also verify the camera at (55,30,55) still frames the particles well when they drift upward past z~80; if they exit the frustum the 'surprise' becomes invisible — a slight camera tilt-up keyed to uAntiGrav would keep the action in frame without violating the fixed-camera preference.

v2.feedback: Strong concept — Lorenz butterfly dissolving into upward drift is a genuine anti-gravity swerve from the parent attractor. Palette (smoke/bone/rust/amber) is well-chosen and the 30s ramp is appropriately contemplative. Two concerns for refinement: once anti-gravity fully engages, the lifted particles likely scatter into an amorphous cloud — consider constraining the drift phase with a soft cylindrical or helical envelope so the dissolution reads as 'ascending form' rather than 'diffusing gas'. Also, the per-particle sinusoidal lateral wander (sin(p.z*0.04)) could use a second harmonic or curl-noise channel at very low amplitude to avoid visible banding in the drift trajectories.
